problems.title: Integral-eigenvalue purity is not stable under allowed positive Tate twists

location.dependency: Theorem4.53 proof, PDF41/printed40; Corollaries4.54 and4.58, PDF42-43

problems.claim: Every R^i Gamma_rig(M) for every M in full H_k over finite k is pure under the definition requiring algebraic-integer eigenvalues.
assumptions: K=K0=Q_2 complete with rational-rank-one value group
M=M(Spec F_2){1}=1(1)[2] lies in H_k because all integer twists are allowed
Witt Frobenius on Q_2 is identity
Exact monoidal realization pins 1(-1) to eigenvalue2, hence inverse twist to1/2
problems.proof: The sole nonzero graded piece of R Gamma_rig(M)=Q_2(1)[2] has eigenvalue1/2. A monic integral polynomial for1/2, after multiplication by2^m, gives odd integer1+2a_(m-1)+...+2^m a0=0, contradiction modulo2. Thus this piece is not pure of any weight under the printed integrality condition, although its complex absolute value is2^(-2/2).
counterevidence_checked: Actual source images confirmed word and quantifiers.
Frobenius inversion does not evade Remark4.41's explicit convention.
Effective-only interpretation changes the stated full Chow heart.
problems.impact: False universal premise explicitly invoked in core Theorem4.53 proof, then Cor4.54/4.58. Major applies to invalid derivation; final comparison not disproved.
problems.correction: Replace algebraic integer by nonzero algebraic number with all complex absolute values q^(w/2). Tate twist shifts weight by -2r. Different-weight spectra are disjoint, so Hom=0; equal finite Q_p dimensions in the two-term complex then give Ext1=0.
problems.repair_verification: Explicit Tate stability and needed spectral Hom/Ext argument checked; complete comparison/Weil input not re-proved.

check.independent_reasoning: For k=F2 and K=Q2, M=1(1)[2] belongs to the explicitly non-effective Chow heart. The fixed arithmetic convention sends 1(-1) to eigenvalue2, so tensor inversion sends M to Q2(1)[2] with eigenvalue1/2. A monic integral equation yields 1=0 mod2 after clearing denominators. Thus the printed algebraic-integer purity premise fails. Theorem4.53 explicitly applies it to every M in H_k before Cor4.38. This is an invalid core derivation, not a counterexample to the comparison theorem. Replacing integrality by the nonzero algebraic-number weight condition preserves Tate stability; different weights give disjoint spectra, Hom=0, and equal finite dimensions in the two-term complex give Ext1=0. Full geometric comparison inputs were not reproved.

problems.title: Infinite product cannot supply claimed canonical ordinary internal coalgebra
problems.claim: Arbitrary lax fixed points are ordinary comodules over product_n t^n, using the comonadic argument.
assumptions: C=D(Q), usual derived tensor: stable,presentable,Q-linear,compactly generated
X=direct sum Qe_j and S(e_j)=e_(j+1) are allowed arbitrary-operator data
problems.proof: Actual right-adjoint comonad G(X)=product_n X. Canonical (product Q) tensor X -> product X has only sequences in a common finite-dimensional subspace, excluding orbit(e_n). Canonical comultiplication at1 sends a_n to a_(i+j); a_n=1/(n+1) gives infinite Hilbert matrix. Its m-by-m blocks have quadratic form integral_0^1(sum c_i x^i)^2>0, hence unbounded rank, whereas any tensor image has finite rank. Therefore canonical comultiplication fails to factor through ordinary tensor.
counterevidence_checked: Completed-tensor/pro interpretation absent in the text; would require changed definitions.
FG3.5.2 and GRChapter6 2.7 distinguish product right-lax formula and true comonad.
problems.impact: Section2.5 explicitly unused later; core theorem uses directsum/ind-nilpotent objects. No demonstrated central dependency.
problems.correction: Retain coalgebras for actual comonad G, not ordinary internal comodules over its value at1; completion alternative unverified.
problems.repair_verification: Ordinary D(Q) comonad formulation checked; no claimed general completed replacement.

check.independent_reasoning: In D(Q), t=Q is compact, Alt2(t)=0 and tensoring with t preserves products. The right-adjoint comonad is product_n X. For X=direct sum Q e_j the orbit(e_n) has no finite common span and is not in (product Q) tensor X. For a_n=1/(n+1), the Hankel blocks are positive definite by integral_0^1 (sum c_i x^i)^2, so their unbounded rank also prevents the proposed ordinary internal comultiplication. Comonadicity is not refuted. The text labels this section unused later; the core ind-nilpotent case uses a direct sum. Hence no central dependency has been established.

problems.title: Mixed Hodge semisimplicity and all-intersection purity criterion are false
subitems: P3a nonsplit extension in graded-polarizable MHS
P3b Tate structure contradicts off-diagonal intersection vanishing
problems.claim: Rational polarizable mixed Hodge category is semisimple; F^p V intersect conjugate(F^q V) vanishes whenever p+q differs from pure weight.
assumptions: E_Q=Qe0+Qe1; W below-2 zero, W_-2 through-1=Qe1, W>=0=E
Weight graded pieces are polarizable types(-1,-1) and(0,0)
problems.proof: The exact sequence0->Q(1)->E->Q(0)->0 has no rational filtration-preserving section: s(1)=e0+a e1 requires a=i. This disproves mixed-category semisimplicity. For own pure Q(1) example F^-2=V, so intersection at(-2,-2) equalsV nonzero despite sum=-4 != -2. Both mathematical assertions fail as written.
counterevidence_checked: Mixed graded-polarizability is distinct from pure semisimplicity.
Root viewed page44 image, including overbar and all off-diagonal quantifier.
Drew1511.08288v1 p9 separately consulted, not falsely identified with source [Dre17].
problems.impact: Local Hodge explanation wrong. Core p-adic theorem does not use mixed-category semisimplicity; Example3.31 actually needs weaker hdim and weight-direction Ext hypotheses.
problems.correction: Use hdim1 and weight-direction Hom/Ext vanishing in graded-polarizable MHS, pure fixed-weight semisimplicity. For pure weightn use V_C=F^p directsum conjugate(F^(n-p+1)); define intersection Hodge summands on p+q=n only.
problems.repair_verification: Explicit nonsplit object, Tate criterion and splitting of extension of weighti by weightj>i via W_iE checked. Entire realization not reconstructed.

check.independent_reasoning: The two rational graded Tate pieces in the given extension are polarizable. A rational F0-preserving section would require the rational coefficient a=i, so the mixed category is not semisimple. On the source own Q(1), F^-2=V makes the (-2,-2) intersection nonzero although its sum differs from weight-2. Opposite filtrations give the correct pure criterion. The actual Example3.31 requires weaker homological-dimension and directed weight Ext vanishing, with W_iE providing the required higher-weight extension splitting. This local Hodge exposition is not an input to the central p-adic proof.
